item.research_question: What are the high-temperature oxidation properties of high-entropic alloys (HEAs) and how can their resistance to oxidation be improved?
item.test_conditions: high-temperature oxidation in air, with some experiments in supercritical water or other atmospheres
key_findings: HEAs based on the Al-Co-Cr-Fe-Ni system show promising resistance to high-temperature oxidation
Additions of Si, Ti, Y, and Hf can improve the resistance of HEAs to high-temperature gas corrosion
Mo additions have a negative effect on corrosion resistance due to the formation of volatile oxides
Al and Cr are key elements in forming continuous films that prevent oxygen diffusion into the alloy matrix
Refractory elements can increase the strength of HEAs at high temperatures but may accelerate oxidation
item.mechanism: The formation of protective oxide layers, such as Al2O3 and Cr2O3, is crucial in preventing further oxidation of the alloy
item.limitations: The study of high-temperature oxidation of HEAs is largely empirical, with limited use of thermodynamic modeling tools
item.future_work: Further research is needed to understand the mechanisms of high-temperature oxidation in HEAs and to develop new corrosion-resistant alloys
quotes: HEAs based on light elements and lanthanides, taking into account the properties of the elements that form them, are oxidized easily and completely

records.text: Paper card. Question: What are the high-temperature oxidation properties of high-entropic alloys (HEAs) and how can their resistance to oxidation be improved?. System: Al-Co-Cr-Fe-Ni, Mn-Co-Cr-Fe-Ni, and refractory HEAs. Test conditions: high-temperature oxidation in air, with some experiments in supercritical water or other atmospheres. Findings: HEAs based on the Al-Co-Cr-Fe-Ni system show promising resistance to high-temperature oxidation; Additions of Si, Ti, Y, and Hf can improve the resistance of HEAs to high-temperature gas corrosion; Mo additions have a negative effect on corrosion resistance due to the formation of volatile oxides; Al and Cr are key elements in forming continuous films that prevent oxygen diffusion into the alloy matrix; Refractory elements can increase the strength of HEAs at high temperatures but may accelerate oxidation. Mechanism: The formation of protective oxide layers, such as Al2O3 and Cr2O3, is crucial in preventing further oxidation of the alloy. Limitations: The study of high-temperature oxidation of HEAs is largely empirical, with limited use of thermodynamic modeling tools. Future work: Further research is needed to understand the mechanisms of high-temperature oxidation in HEAs and to develop new corrosion-resistant alloys. Quote: "HEAs based on light elements and lanthanides, taking into account the properties of the elements that form them, are oxidized easily and completely"
